utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise what this man is wearing?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: No. No, it's difficult for me to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we keep playing a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voice-over] A handful of people gave us a good running around. That, that moron over there. Here. Where is he? Where did they move him? There he is. That one. [Expletive] ... that one there. There he is. He is going over there."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, we saw two video-clips here, and can you just -- you told us earlier that the -- the clothing that you saw on the first clip was the type of the person you saw at the JNA barracks, and we also saw the way that people were addressing. Is this what you also experimented [sic] at the JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: It's hard to make the connections, but there is a resemblance. If I try to describe them, I would describe them as a crowd on a rampage. Not exactly, perhaps, but close to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you recognise any of the locations on the two clips that we just saw?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: The first location was in town near Becarski Kriz. And the second location, I suppose, is in Borovo Naselje, on the Borovo road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I ask that the two clips marked as 4989.3 and 4799.4 be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, you only -- you tender them only for the images or for the images and -- because there are no transcript in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The transcripts are available, Your Honours. I have been just informed that they just need to be linked. So perhaps for the time we can MFI them and once the case manager contacts the court officer we can finalize this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I agree with that. So we'll -- we'll mark them for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter document 4989.3 shall be assigned Exhibit P1401 marked for identification. And 65 ter document 4799.4 shall be assigned Exhibit P1402, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like to take you back to the barracks. While you were on the buses, were the two soldiers you indicated to us which were on the bus earlier at the Vukovar Hospital, were they still on the bus?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Yes. They were our protection escorts on the journey, and they were with us all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And how long did the buses remain at the JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I said, an hour, perhaps two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Were you able to tell at what time the buses departed the JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I suppose it was between 1.00 and 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And how were you able to tell the time on that day?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: At that time I still had a watch and I looked at it from time to time, and I was able to also know the time because it was a sunny day and you could deduce even without a watch what the time was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, where did the buses drive to next?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Before the buses left -- I think I've already mentioned that two or three more buses joined us from the direction of Sajmiste. And after this long motorcade was formed, the vehicles drove a full circle, a return to Sajmiste, and continued towards Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did the buses go to Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: No. Before Negoslavci they took a left turn to a former track that had been paved in the meantime and was used by agricultural machines that were used for agricultural production.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when they turned left, where did they head to?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: They took a shortcut towards a large farm known as Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Were you familiar with this area?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Yes, I know that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And just bear with me, can you tell -- I'm sorry. Can you tell the Court how you were familiar with the area of Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I spent time there during the spring. I knew that area very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, when the buses arrived at Ovcara, which bus were you on?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: In the second or third bus. After I boarded, nothing changed. I remained in the same position. Because the buses that joined us, joined us from the tail.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, when the buses arrived at Ovcara, did they stop anywhere?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: They stopped by the hangar which was a warehouse for agricultural tools and other equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, what -- what happened once the buses stopped by the hangar?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: We started getting off. People got off the buses one by one, and they went into that hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court how the buses were unloaded? When you say that the people got off the buses one by one, can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: One by one. A line was formed to get off the buses. People got out one by one because you know how narrow the door on the bus is. After one bus was emptied, the next bus in line would move up, and that's how everybody got out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, in your bus, on which side of the bus were you sitting?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: On the right-hand side in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: When the buses stopped in front of the hangar, were you able to see if there was anyone outside?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I saw soldiers and reservists or whatever they were. I saw them walking to and fro and standing around the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you give the Judges a rough idea of number of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Well, there were certainly around 50. Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, what happened next? Once people were unloading the buses, what would happen next?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: People were directed to the hangar. Clothes were removed from them. All the valuables they had were taken. If they were holding something in their hands, they would have to throw it on a heap, and they were pushed into the hangar. Herded into the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what happens once prisoners entered the hangar?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Upon entering the hangar, the prisoners had to walk through a gauntlet made up of those soldiers who were present. They were beaten with various objects and pushed into the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: How many soldiers were there in this -- forming this gauntlet?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Around 20. Although it's difficult to say precisely now but around 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the soldiers when you exited the bus?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: While I was still on the bus, I noticed Dusan Borovac, for instance, who was a reservist. I recognised him. But I could not remember now anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm wondering whether we should redact the last two lines to be on the safe side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please do, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you explained to us that prisoners had to go through a gauntlet and were beaten with objects. Once you entered the hangar and you passed the gauntlet, where did you go to next?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: After the gauntlet and all the commotion there, we were placed on the hay. There was hay all over the hangar. Some people sat down; some were still standing. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Were the prisoners received in -- in the hangar in any way?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: No. They were beaten up in that gauntlet. And, after that, they freely dispersed in the first half of that hangar on top of the hay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you give the Chamber a rough estimate of how many prisoners there were in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Judging by the number of buses that I saw and taking into account how many people one bus can hold and from seeing how many we were inside the hangar, my estimate would be around 300 prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, after the commotion of the gauntlet, which you explained to us, could you tell the Court how the detainees were treated inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: After that torture we went through, people were abused individually. Those groups of men - or, rather, not humans - would pick on individuals and beat them up, some of them to death.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the prisoners who were treated this way?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Yes. Very close to me was the man known as Kemo who was so badly beaten, kicked beaten with rifle-butts and barrels, that the only conclusion I -- I can make is that he -- he died there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Is this the only prisoner that you remember who was treated this way?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: No. I also remember Vladimir Djukic, nicknamed Dado, who was beaten with baseball bats and even with his own crutches. He had been recently wounded and shot in his legs, so he was using crutches, and they used those crutches to beat him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you give us an idea of how many prisoners were being beaten inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: It's hard to say. It was chaotic. Visibility was bad because there was so many people inside. But we can take it that at least 10 per cent of those people were badly beaten and mistreated in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you specify who was doing the beating?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Well, those were reservists and troops who were there. Members of the army who were within the compound in the hangar, abusing prisoners. The army, the JNA, whatever you want to call them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you notice whether anyone was in charge inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: There was a person, a man, stocky, with a moustache, wearing a JNA windcheater with rank insignia and a whistle, and with that whistle, he somehow supervised those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And how was he supervising these individuals?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Well, he blew his whistle to somehow diminish the abuse that was going on, and after his warnings, the violence would die down. They would leave. But very soon, they would come back, and the same thing would go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, when you -- when you exited the buses, you told us that you saw about 50 soldiers outside. Are you able to tell us whether it was the same group that entered the hangar?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that, but it's highly likely that they, too, went in and committed misdeeds.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, were you questioned by anyone inside the hangar at one point?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I personally was not questioned by anyone, but they did list us all. So I was addressed eventually by that person who was making a list of all us in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you tell us what was being put on that list.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: They took down our personal details, date and place of birth, names of parents, and address, as far as I can remember. At any rate, the soldier who was making that list went around and listed us all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, I would like to have the assistance of the usher to -- if you could draw on the screen a diagram of the hangar on a blank screen. I will ask you to use different colours just so that we could distinguish persons and locations. So could we first have maybe a blank screen in front of us. Thank you very much. Now, sir, using perhaps the -- I don't know, we have three or four colours. Let's use the blue colour first, if possible. And can you first draw the hangar.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you -- all right. Yes. Now what's that smaller rectangle you drew at the bottom right?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: It's one of the entrances into the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you first mark -- could you first mark the entrance with the letter A.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. You can erase that and do it again if it's not clear enough. Yes, let's erase that writing at the bottom. Thank you. Now, below the entrance, below A, what do we see there?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: It's the access to the hangar and the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Could you mark the access with the letter B.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, when you entered the hangar, could you show us where the gauntlet was and mark that with the letter C.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you went -- you were all aligned in one part of the hangar, occupying half of that hangar. Could you show us where that was, where the men were lined up?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And could you maybe mark that general area with the letter D.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Was there anything separating the men, or were they all in one long file?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: There was a school desk there which had one end of the rope tied to it. And the rope stretched to the other end. And this is where some of the prisoners were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Maybe using a different colour, if you could use the colour red, could we draw that desk and the rope, please.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And can you put the letter E for the desk, please.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you show us where you were once you went through the gauntlet? And use the letter F.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You told us that you saw Kemo being beaten. Where was he located? And can you use a letter G for that.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And you also mentioned Dado Djukic. Where was he located? Letter H. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you show us where you saw the -- the -- the soldier or the officer with the moustache and the whistle? And use the letter I.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, finally, you told us that you noticed Dusan Borovac. Where was he when you noticed him? Put the letter J.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I saw him outside the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This was while you were on the bus still; correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And inside the hangar, did you recognise any other soldier?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I recognised some soldiers in the hangar though.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I meant. Sorry. Can you tell us who you recognised in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I recognised some locals, most of them from Sajmiste. I particularly observed Miroljub and some others whose names I can't recall at present.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know Miroljub's last name?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I have to give it a think ... Perhaps I'll remember later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's fine. When you saw him in the hangar, what was he wearing on that day?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: He was wearing a grey olive-green uniform and a cap that was somewhat peculiar compared to that which was normally worn by the reservists. It was more like a baseball cap with the -- with the long brim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you remember if Miroljub had any role or function at the time?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: It was hard to tell who had which function, but he did leave the impression of having a significant role.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And this man named Miroljub, did you hear of him after the war?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Yes. He was accused and perhaps has been convicted in the meantime for the crime at Ovcara. I think that he is in prison now, in Belgrade or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I tender the drawing that the witness made on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The hand-drawn sketch will be assigned exhibit number P1403. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: With the help of the usher -- first of all, could we display on the screen 65 ter 5846, which is at tab 66. And we can go to page 11, please, in the B/C/S version. Thank you very much. If we can zoom in just a little bit. Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, this is a list of victims which was annexed to the indictment in this case. Could I ask you to go through the names that you see on the screen and indicate for us whether you recognise anyone. And, as you recognise someone, we will be marking them with letters, as to whether you know that they took part in -- during the conflict, whether they were civilians. If you don't know, we'll use certain letters. So could you first tell us if, on this page, you're able to recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Tomislav Bajnrauh. He lived in my neighbourhood. I don't know what his participation was in the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you put a question mark next to his name. Yes. Can you now put a question mark next to his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's not working? There's no way to mark this ... Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you put a question mark next to his name? I only see a dot here.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So that is Tomislav Bajnrauh. Anybody else on this page?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Stjepan Balas, right beneath him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you know what he did during the war?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, before we move on, these two individuals, did you know them or did you see them? Could you tell us about them, please.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I didn't see Bajnrauh, if we are talking about Ovcara. As for Stjepan Balas, he was next to me, or close to me, within the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I apologise, sir, I believe my question may have been a little unclear. What I want you to do is only mark the persons that you saw either at the hospital, on your bus, or at Ovcara on that day. So Bajnrauh, did you see him on that day or not?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I didn't see him on that day. Bajnrauh. You asked me if I knew anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise. I only want you to mark on this list those that you saw on the 20th of November. Going down that list, is there anybody else that you recognise -- that you -- sorry. That you saw on that day, on the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Nobody else on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Before we move to the next page, is it possible to capture the markings? I will admit the whole list -- do I have to tender each page one by one?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It can be captured. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Are you able to see the page? Yes.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Again, on this page, if you could mark -- first of all, tell us if you recognise anybody you saw on the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: For instance, Vladimir Djukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, you did mention him earlier. What was his role or function during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: He was the commander at the front line at Sajmiste. At one of the positions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Can we put the letter D next to his name, for defender.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Stanko Duvnjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: He was in the hospital. I also saw him at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And was he a defender or -- do you know?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He was a defender within the Ministry of Interior. He was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you put the letter D next to his name.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if you can carry down that list.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Dragan Gavric.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what about him? What was his status?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: In the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you put a question mark next to his name.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Carry down that list.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Sinisa Glavasevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what was he during the conflict? What was his role.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: He was a journalist from Vukovar. He worked as a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did he take part in -- during the combat?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: He did not. He was reporting on the situation at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could I ask you to put the letter C next to his name, which we will use for civilian.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And as you go through this list, I will ask you to use these three letters - the D, the C, and the question mark - depending on what your knowledge is. Is there anybody else on this list?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Drago Gudlej.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Where did you see him on that day?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: In the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what was his function?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Use the question mark then.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Is there anybody else?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let's capture these markings and move to the next page, please. Can we zoom in just a little bit. Yeah. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, can we use the same letters on this page, sir.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Can we have the next list?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Before we move. Zeljko Jurela. Where did you see him on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: He was with me on the bus. And even in the military vehicle that took us outside the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let's move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, if you can carry on with this page as well.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Can we have the next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] yes.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You put a question mark next to Mato Perak. Can you tell us where you saw him on that day?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: He was with me as we were leaving the hangar and boarding the military vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Is there anybody else on this page?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. I believe there's one more page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, if you can carry on with this page as well.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And we see you put a question mark next to Ceman Saiti. Who is he?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Based on the information I have now, I can assume that this is the man going by the nickname of Kemo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You have placed a D next to Damjan Samardzic. Can you tell us where you saw him?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I saw him on the bus, on the trip that started from the compound of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. If you move down that list.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Tadija Tadic. Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I saw him in the hospital. He had just been wounded and was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: I don't recognise anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, if you can tell us whether you recognise anybody on this page that you had seen on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Where did you see Zvonko Varenica?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: In the hangar. He was close to me. He was a maintenance worker in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did he take part in the combat?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: No, I don't have knowledge to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you move down the list.

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: That will be all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask to -- may I tender the marked versions of this list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Pages 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, and 17 of the 65 ter document 5846 marked by the witness shall be assigned exhibit number 1404. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And before we adjourn for the day --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us how long you remained in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: How long? Well, an hour, two, three. It's difficult to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what happened after this time that you were in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: GH-080
utterances.text: Since it became dark soon after, quite soon, the evacuation of the prisoners from -- from the hangar began.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. We'll continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think this is an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Demirdjian. Mr. Witness, this brings us to the end of the today's hearing. You are not released as a witness. You will come back tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the same courtroom. In the meantime, you are -- you're still under oath, which means that you're not allowed to discuss with anybody your testimony and that are you not allowed to talk to any of the parties in the meantime. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We -- thank you. We will go into closed session now, and then the court usher will escort you out of court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 6th day of March, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.
